This run swept the NOT-yet-touched files in the segment: jwt.rs, auth.rs, auth_policy.rs, totp.rs, oauth.rs, stripe.rs, notification.rs, notification_digest.rs, quiet_hours{,_drain}.rs, feature_service.rs, accounting.rs, id_ocr.rs, and the untouched api-core extractors/middleware (host_tenant.rs, principal.rs, extractors/auth.rs, tenant.rs, security_headers.rs, tenanted_redis.rs, feature_guard.rs, authorization.rs, tenant_filter.rs). Static-only Rust review: grep sweep for unwrap()/expect() outside #[cfg(test)] modules, todo!()/unimplemented!(), then targeted reads. Verdict: this cluster is heavily hardened — jwt.rs/stripe.rs/oauth.rs/auth_policy.rs/host_tenant.rs all show deliberate, well-commented security design (constant-time HMAC compare via ct_eq, PKCE S256-only, fail-closed RLS/rate-limit/CORS defaults, OS-RNG-failure panics that are an accepted crypto idiom, not a bug); every unwrap()/expect() hit outside tests was either on a provably-infallible input (hardcoded Decimal literals, a static well-formed HTTP response, NonZeroU32 after .max(1)) or the deliberate fail-closed RNG panic. Two genuine findings survived verification, both in notification.rs (used live by services/scheduler/mod.rs + scheduler/votes.rs for vote/announcement/payment-due notifications — not a dead/legacy path).
note: api-core (backend/servers/api-server/src/services + backend/crates/api-core). Top finding: NotificationService's in-memory dedup cache has a fixed 5-minute rolling TTL re-armed on every send, but send_vote_reminders() re-selects the same not-yet-voted users on every 60s scheduler tick for up to vote_reminder_days_before=1 day — so a user who hasn't voted gets the identical 'Reminder: Vote on X' push+in-app notification roughly every 5 minutes, up to ~288 times, for the full 24h window before the vote closes. Second finding: NotificationChannel::Push in the same service is a permanent no-op (logs 'integration pending', never calls a real provider) on a channel users can explicitly opt into per-event via granular preferences (pref.push_enabled) and that notify_payment_due/notify_vote_reminder/etc. explicitly request — a parallel, unwired push path distinct from the real FCM-integrated push_fanout.rs system already flagged separately on 2026-08-28. Both are static-analysis findings (traced call path from scheduler wiring through to the bug; not runtime-confirmed) in a segment that is otherwise unusually well-hardened.

evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/scheduler/mod.rs:262-288 — Scheduler::start() ticks every SchedulerConfig.interval_secs (default 60s, :81 'Check every minute') and calls run_scheduled_tasks() unconditionally on every tick.
backend/servers/api-server/src/services/scheduler/mod.rs:337-339 — run_scheduled_tasks() calls self.send_vote_reminders().await on EVERY tick, with no once-per-day or once-per-vote gating.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/scheduler/votes.rs:442-461 — send_vote_reminders() re-runs the SAME stateless query every tick: 'SELECT * FROM votes WHERE status = 'active' AND end_at <= $1 AND end_at > NOW()' (cutoff = now + vote_reminder_days_before days, default 1 — mod.rs:83). No column (e.g. last_reminded_at) is read or written to record that a vote/user pair was already reminded, so the exact same (vote, not-voted-user) set is re-selected on the next tick 60s later, and the tick after that, for the entire ~24h 'ending soon' window.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/scheduler/votes.rs:475-483 calls notification_service.notify_vote_reminder(&vote, &users_not_voted) every time the vote is selected — i.e. every ~60s while the vote remains active and ending within the window.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/notification.rs:177-197 (should_deduplicate) + :199-223 (record_sent) — the ONLY anti-spam mechanism is an in-memory HashMap keyed by (user_id, notification_type, entity_id) with a rolling window: record_sent overwrites `sent_at = Utc::now()` on every successful (non-deduped) send, and should_deduplicate only suppresses while `Utc::now() - entry.sent_at < dedup_window_secs` (default 300s = 5 minutes, :116). Because the window re-arms from the LAST send rather than the FIRST, and because the underlying scheduler condition ('has this user voted yet?') stays true across many ticks, the cache limits delivery to at most once per 5 minutes — not once total. At a 60s tick and a 300s window, the notification re-fires roughly every 5th tick, i.e. ~12 times/hour, up to ~288 times over the default 24h reminder window, per non-voted user per vote.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/notification.rs:662 — notify_vote_reminder's channels are `vec![NotificationChannel::InApp, NotificationChannel::Push]`, both of which fire on every re-send (before accounting for the separate Push no-op finding below), so a voting user gets repeated in-app badge/list entries and (if the Push path were wired) repeated push pings for the same vote.

Contrast: sibling dispatch_vote_started_notifications / dispatch_vote_closed_notifications / dispatch_announcement_notifications (mod.rs:298-303, 330-335, 300-303 comments) are explicitly 'decoupled... so a transient failure retries next tick', implying they gate on a one-time state transition (activate/close, a DB flag flips exactly once) — send_vote_reminders is structurally different (a persisting-until-resolved condition) and was never given the equivalent DB-level once-per-window tracking that pattern implies for the others.

Fix direction: either (a) persist a `last_reminded_at` (or a `vote_reminders_sent` join row) per (vote_id, user_id) and only remind once per configurable cadence (e.g. once per day, or exactly once at the vote_reminder_days_before mark) directly in the SQL WHERE clause, mirroring how the activate/close paths use a DB state flip as their own dedup; or (b) at minimum widen the in-memory dedup window to exceed vote_reminder_days_before so a single reminder truly is single per vote (note this still would not fix multi-replica deployments, since the cache is per-process). Confidence high: full path traced from the 60s ticker through the stateless re-selecting query to the re-arming in-memory cache; the math (60s tick / 300s window) is read directly from the two config defaults, not inferred.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-08-30 api-core notification push stub)
evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/notification.rs:348-356 — inside send_to_user's per-channel match, the NotificationChannel::Push arm is: `// Push notifications would integrate with FCM/APNs. For now, just log. tracing::info!(...'Push notification (integration pending)')` — it never calls any push provider; every Push-channel notification silently 'succeeds' (the outer function still logs 'Notification sent' and returns Ok(())) without ever being delivered.

This is a LIVE production path, not dead code: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/scheduler/mod.rs:166-169 constructs `Arc<NotificationService>` and wires it into the background Scheduler; scheduler/votes.rs:480 (notify_vote_reminder) and scheduler/mod.rs:1066/1152 (notify_payment_due, overdue and due-soon) and :491 (notify_announcement_published) and :986 (notify_meter_reading_due) all call through this exact NotificationService instance on every scheduler tick.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/notification.rs:227-244 (is_channel_enabled) reads a REAL, user-controllable preference — `pref.push_enabled` from GranularNotificationRepository::get_user_event_preference — to decide whether to attempt the Push branch, so a user who explicitly turns on push notifications for e.g. payment-due or vote-reminder events in their settings gets routed straight into the no-op stub with no error, no fallback, and no signal anywhere that the channel never fired.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/notification.rs:632 (notify_payment_due, channels includes Push alongside InApp+Email — so Email/InApp mask the gap there) and :662 (notify_vote_reminder, channels is ONLY `[InApp, Push]` — no Email fallback) — a user who relies on push (the common case for a mobile-first voting/PM app) and has push_enabled=true for vote reminders gets NO delivered notification at all for that event type, only a silently-dropped one.

Contrast: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/push_fanout.rs (2124 lines, already flagged for a stale-OAuth-token issue on 2026-08-28, confirming it IS a real, wired FCM integration) is a completely separate, parallel push-delivery system that NotificationService::send_to_user never delegates to — the codebase has a working push pipeline, this legacy/duplicate path just never got hooked up to it.

Fix direction: replace the Push match arm with a call into the same push-dispatch path push_fanout.rs uses (or have NotificationService construct/enqueue through PushFanoutWorker's queue instead of sending inline), so the two push systems converge on one implementation; at minimum, until wired, is_channel_enabled should short-circuit Push to `false` (or log at warn!, not silently swallow) so this doesn't read to callers as 'delivered'. Confidence high: the stub is unambiguous (a log-only comment naming the exact gap), and the call path from scheduler → NotificationService → Push arm is fully traced through live (not test-only) code, corroborated by the granular per-event push_enabled preference existing specifically to gate this now-inert branch.
